newsitem.title: FRANCE: French colonel denies recruiting Zaire mercenaries.
newsitem.headline: French colonel denies recruiting Zaire mercenaries.

text.p: A former security chief at the French presidency has denied that he he is putting together a mercenary force to help the government of Zaire fight Rwandan-backed rebels.

"Such allegations cast doubts on my honour and I wonder who can benefit from such a manipulation," Alain Le Caro, a colonel in the para-military gendarmerie who left the service in 1994, told the daily Le Monde on Wednesday.

The same newspaper reported a day earlier that he was in charge of recruiting a "White Legion" of several hundred European and African mercenaries. Le Caro said he was neither directly nor indirectly involved with soldiers of fortune.

In a separate interview with the conservative daily Le Figaro, Le Caro said he had no ties to Zaire's leaders and had not even visited the country since 1982. "Furthermore, I'm in Paris and not in Zaire, as Le Monde claims," he said.

Le Caro, head of the presidential guard at the Elysee palace during late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand's rule, said he worked as an advisor to the governments of Burkina Faso and the Ivory Coast.

He told Le Monde, which corrected the spelling of his surname from "Carro", that he believed he upset "wheeler-dealer groups involved in Africa" and "ill-intentioned people, who accuse me, in a veiled way, of acting against French interests".

Le Monde alleged that he was working in Zaire with another former gendarme, Robert Montoya, who carried out anti-terrorism missions for the presidency and was involved in a wiretap scandal before leaving the service 10 years ago.
Le Monde said Montoya also denied its report, saying he had never been to Zaire and that he merely represented French companies.

On Tuesday, Le Monde said the force numbered between 200 and 300 but was expected to grow rapidly when more men leave Europe in two weeks to join South African, French, Belgian, British, Angolan and Mozambican soldiers of fortune on the spot.

On Tuesday, French Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain said there were mercenaries from some European nations in the region but denied any official French involvement, saying Paris was the victim of a media smear campaign.
Le Caro also said that "recruitment of mercenaries doesn't surprise me."
"In Africa there are indeed a certain number of mercenaries who travel round and are taken up by this agency or that," he told Europe 1 radio.

The French presidency said it had no connection with, or knowledge of, a mercenary force. France backs Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko politically but an international arms embargo on Zaire bars any military aid.
